top.title: ‘I didn’t tell them to go buy votes,’ Wike defends N10m reward for councillors
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said he never asked councillors to buy votes with the N10 million he promised those who deliver their wards in the 2027 general elections. “I didn’t tell them, ‘Take this money and go and buy votes.’ I said, ‘Go and work. Show commitment. Demonstrate that you really mean what you are talking about. When you win, come, and we are going to reward you,” he said. Wike spoke on Tuesday during an inspection of ongoing infrastructure projects in Abuja. He was responding to criticism of the promise, which he said was an incentive for hard work and not an attempt to buy votes. Addressing stakeholders, traditional leaders, and political actors in Kwali Area Council the previous day, Wike had explained that the initiative was part of a broad grassroots mobilisation strategy designed to rally maximum support at the grassroots level. “For the councillors, you have a task. I will hold a meeting with you again, and I will now say the way I am going to mobilise you, but I will give you a bet, like what is happening in the stars; it’s a competition. “Anybody who delivers his ward, if you deliver your ward, that is what the Rainbow Coalition has decided to do as mobilisation and support for Mr President; we have to start in the FCT (I couldn’t say so when the president came because they gave me only two minutes to talk). But now that I have time to talk, let me say that the Rainbow Coalition all over the federation, as a form of mobilisation for Mr President to win this election, is saying that any councillor that delivers his ward will come and take N10 million. We want to mobilise for Mr President. So, go to your wards, and go and see your leaders. I know only you cannot do it, but we are using you as an instrumentality for your leaders. Go and meet your leaders and say, ‘Look, oh, there is something that has come.’ We must not allow this thing to go. Let’s dedicate our ward for Mr President’. So, that is for that,” Wike had said. Speaking on Tuesday, Wike drew a line between rewarding political commitment and offering money to voters in exchange for their support. He said the councillors were challenged to prove their commitment through effective mobilisation. To make his case, he pointed to athletes who are promised houses or other benefits if they return from international competitions with trophies. He asked why a similar reward in politics should automatically be read as bribery. He also faulted sections of the media for failing to tell legitimate rewards apart from vote-buying. Political parties and candidates, he argued, routinely spend money on campaign advertisements without facing the same scrutiny. Wike urged journalists to pay closer attention to the difference between financial inducements meant to sway voters and rewards promised to political mobilisers for hitting set targets. top.title: French Students Block Dozens Of Schools
top.description: French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, the education ministry said, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions. Student protests across France since September have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by fringe violence and accusations of police brutality. The unrest comes ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron next year. With the European Union’s second biggest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Students dance in front of police officers during a rally over learning conditions as part of a nationwide day of action, as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Paris on November 5, 2026. Forty-nine of the country’s 3,700 high schools for 15- to 18-year-olds were blockaded on Tuesday morning, the ministry said. Authorities expected several thousand school and university students at a Paris protest on Tuesday afternoon. “Now is the time to step up the mobilisation by continuing to put pressure on the government,” student and teacher unions said in a joint statement released Monday. Student association leader Ryad Rani said it was essential to keep up the pressure. “We’re not just fighting for ourselves. We’re fighting for teachers, for their working conditions,” he said. The government has announced measures including the gradual replacement of an online selection platform to access higher education, as well as financial means for some of the worst-off schools. But students say this is not enough. Unions are not happy either, with one leader saying on Monday that a government pledge to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent on top of a standard adjustment for inflation was “crumbs”. They have called for a new day of strikes and protests on November 17. Around 575,000 people demonstrated across the country during cost-of-living strikes and protests last Thursday, according to authorities. Unions put the number at 1.5 million. top.title: Arsenal 31yo makes World 11, teammate narrowly misses out
top.description: Arsenal 31yo makes World 11, teammate narrowly misses out David Raya has become the first Arsenal player to feature in the FIFPRO World 11 since Thierry Henry, with a couple of his teammates only narrowly missing out. Photo via FIFPRO on Instagram After tallying up 19,806 votes from professional men’s footballers across 73 countries, FIFPRO named their World 11 on Monday night, with Arsenal’s David Raya making the cut. Raya is the first Arsenal player to be included in the World 11 since Thierry Henry in 2006, and he’s one of just two Premier League players in the 2026 side alongside Erling Haaland (or three if you include Rodri ). It wasn’t a close race in the goalkeeper position, with Raya receiving more than 2,500 more votes than his nearest competitor. In fact, the goalkeeper received more votes than anyone else in the entire lineup, with over half of the voters picking him. FIFPRO World 11 for 2026 Arsenal were rather unlucky not to have at least one more player in the lineup. Gabriel Magalhaes received the second-most votes of any centre-back, only behind Pau Cubarsi of Barcelona and Spain. But the award organisers opted to select a team with only three defenders, one of whom was a left-back, and another a right-back. So with only one centre-back spot in the side, Gabriel missed out. If the team used a formation that a real football team might use, Gabriel would have been included, as it’s very hard to think of any team in world football that only uses one centre-back. William Saliba was also very close to making the cut, as both Gabriel and Saliba finished within 1,000 votes of Cubarsi. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Declan Rice was the other Arsenal player to receive a significant quantity of votes, but he wasn’t particularly close to making the final team. Though he received over 3,000 votes, that was around 2,500 short of anyone in the top-three. Raya sent a message to the voters after receiving his award, saying : “Thank you guys for voting me into the FIFPRO World 11. It’s incredible how you guys have voted for me. Thank you very much to everyone that has chosen me to be part of this, and keep doing your thing.” Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

top.title: ‘Y’all wish’ – Luka Doncic responds to Atlanta Hawks heckler with reminder their biggest mistake
top.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Even eight years later, Luka Doncic has not forgotten about how the Atlanta Hawks disrespected him in the NBA Draft. Doncic is now the next superstar for the Los Angeles Lakers, taking over the mantle from LeBron James following his departure earlier this summer. But before he arrived in Los Angeles, Doncic was the name and face of the Dallas Mavericks for seven years, a position carved out for him on the night of the 2018 NBA Draft. Luka Doncic pokes fun at Atlanta Hawks fan over 2018 NBA Draft trade During the Los Angeles Lakers’ win against the Atlanta Hawks, Luka Doncic got into a heated exchange with some hecklers sitting courtside. Doncic used the back-and-forth as an opportunity to remind them that the Hawks made a mistake giving him up in the 2018 NBA Draft. Luka Doncic: “You all wish you would’ve had me. You all wish, huh?” Fan #1: “We had you.” Fan #2: “No, we don’t. I’ve never wanted you.” Fan #3: “I wish we did; I do.” Luka Doncic: “You know you could have had me.” Fan #3: “He’s right.” Of course, Doncic is referencing the draft-night trade the Atlanta Hawks made in 2018. The Hawks had the #3 overall pick in the 2018 NBA Draft, with Doncic being expected to be selected by the Hawks. However, on the night, the Hawks traded the draft rights to Luka Doncic (whom they picked at #3) to the Dallas Mavericks in exchange for the draft rights to Trae Young and a 2019 protected first-round pick that turned out to be Cam Reddish. Fast-forward eight years, and the Hawks have fully given up on Trae Young, trading him to the Washington Wizards earlier this year after an eight-year stint that saw them reach the Eastern Conference Finals just once. As for Cam Reddish, he never adapted to the NBA and found himself outside of the league following the conclusion of the 2024-25 NBA season. In the early days of the trade, many had suggested that the Mavericks and Hawks had pulled off a rare win-win trade. However, following Young’s decline as a superstar, the consensus became clear – the Mavericks had pulled off a coup for Doncic. Unfortunately for the Mavericks, they didn’t get to reap the rewards of their clever trade, as Nico Harrison would trade Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie, and just one first-round pick. Now, the Lakers have emerged as the ultimate winners of a trade in 2018 that never included them in the first place. top.description: Tarik Skubal | © Instagram /@dodgers MLB insider and New York Post columnist Joel Sherman believes Tarik Skubal’s free agency could mirror that of Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who signed the largest pitching contract in MLB history with Los Angeles during the 2023 offseason (12-year, $325 million). Sherman shared his thoughts on the latest episode of ‘The Show’ with co-host Jon Heyman, a fellow MLB insider. Discussing several facets of the ongoing offseason, Sherman began by naming some of the game’s aces before quickly turning to Skubal, saying his free-agent battle could come down to the Mets and Dodgers. Although plenty of teams will be interested in acquiring him, the pursuit could ultimately end much as Yamamoto’s did. “So look, I think they’re, to your point, if we were going to name who’s the ace of the sport, it would be a very short list. Yamamoto, Skubal, maybe Schlittler, like Skubal’s on it, and it might be Skubal, to your point. And he’s free,” Sherman said. “And so I think there’ll be interest in him. And yet I think it’s going to be like Yoshinobu Yamamoto. I think it’s the Mets and the Dodgers. I have yet to talk to an executive or a scout who doesn’t think it’s going to be the Mets versus the Dodgers in this,” he added. Watch the video here: During the campaign’s second half, Skubal and Yamamoto got a taste of what it would be like to team up with another ace. Skubal finished the campaign 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA, 186 strikeouts, and a 0.96 WHIP, while Yamamoto went 14-9 with a 2.53 ERA, 182 strikeouts, and a 0.87 WHIP. They are not in the desperation mode that the Mets are in to get better. I think the Mets are the favorite,” Heyman said. Monday was the first day of the General Managers’ meetings in Las Vegas, and multiple sources already believe the Mets are favorites to land Skubal this offseason. ESPN’s Jeff Passan also believes Skubal is expected to make his free agency decision by Dec. 1, before the current CBA expires. top.title: Konate reveals Kylian Mbappe’s reaction to missing out on Ballon d’Or: ‘He more than deserved it’
top.description: Konate reveals Kylian Mbappe’s reaction to missing out on Ballon d’Or: ‘He more than deserved it’ Kylian Mbappe has wasted little time moving on from his Ballon d’Or disappointment, despite finishing just 28 points behind Harry Kane in the voting. The Real Madrid forward came close to claiming the individual award , but Kane ultimately emerged as the winner. Mbappe has not spoken extensively about the result since the ceremony, with his attention returning to club football. However, France and Real Madrid teammate Ibrahima Konate has offered his insight into how the forward has reacted, suggesting the defeat has not affected his focus or motivation. Konate explains why the defeat hurt Mbappe Konate, who signed for Real Madrid this past summer on a free transfer from Liverpool, suggested that the narrow defeat was particularly difficult for the forward because he believed the award was within his reach. Konate explains why Mbappe was hurt after missing out on the Ballon d’or. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) “He more than deserved the Ballon d’Or, which is why it’s tough for him not to have won it.” The Real Madrid defender added, as per Defensa Central , that “He’s in very good spirits. He’s ready for whatever comes his way and is working hard.” Mbappe answers disappointment with goals Mbappe, on his part, has made a strong start to life after the ceremony. He scored in each of the club’s three subsequent fixtures, finding the net against Racing Santander, AEK Athens and Valencia. Mbappe opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 3-0 victory over Racing, struck in the 3-2 Champions League win against AEK and scored again during the 3-0 success at Valencia. Kylian Mbappe is still enjoying a great run of form. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Notably, the sequence of his form is actually giving him a useful platform for the remainder of the campaign. Rather than allowing the Ballon d’Or result to dominate his season, Mbappe can focus on collective trophies and performances that will influence his next opportunity to win it. UCL success could influence Mbappe’s next Ballon d’Or bid The absence of a major men’s international tournament in 2027 places additional importance on club football in the next Ballon d’Or race. Mbappe will therefore have a significant incentive to help Real Madrid compete for the Champions League and deliver consistently across the season. Indeed, the likes of Lamine Yamal will still be in contention, but if Real Madrid win major trophies under Jose Mourinho, especially the Champions League, Mbappe’s chances of challenging for the Ballon d’Or next year will undoubtedly increase.

top.description: Hungarian federation issues Dominik Szoboszlai update as Liverpool left sweating on his fitness The Hungarian FA has issued an update on the fitness of Dominik Szoboszlai ahead of their upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures. There is an injury concern over the midfielder after he sprained his knee in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday, with Andoni Iraola unsure as to whether or not the 26-year-old would be able to represent his country during this international window. The Magyars are away to Georgia this coming Saturday and then host Northern Ireland three days later in what could be a straight shootout for promotion to League A on the final matchday. Szoboszlai decision to be left to the ‘last minute’ On Tuesday, the Hungarian FA published an update via X in which they confirmed that a decision on Szoboszlai won’t be taken until the latest possible opportunity. They stated: ‘Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations. Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible. ‘However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute.’ (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? However, those of a Liverpool perspective will surely be hoping that Szoboszlai isn’t risked in either game if he isn’t 100% fit to feature, as he’ll be very much needed at Anfield going into the unforgiving winter schedule. The Reds still have 11 more matches to play in 2026, starting with a grudge fixture at home to Manchester United on Sunday week, and squad depth and rotation will be essential during that hectic period in the run-up to Christmas and New Year’s. Having only recently returned from a thigh issue, Andoni Iraola will be hoping that this doesn’t turn into a season of frequent interruptions for the usually dependable Hungarian, who before this autumn hadn’t missed a game through injury since February 2024 ( Transfermarkt ). nigeria.title: French Students Block Dozens Of Schools
nigeria.description: French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, the education ministry said, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions. Student protests across France since September have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by fringe violence and accusations of police brutality. The unrest comes ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron next year. With the European Union’s second biggest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Students dance in front of police officers during a rally over learning conditions as part of a nationwide day of action, as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Paris on November 5, 2026. Forty-nine of the country’s 3,700 high schools for 15- to 18-year-olds were blockaded on Tuesday morning, the ministry said. Authorities expected several thousand school and university students at a Paris protest on Tuesday afternoon. “Now is the time to step up the mobilisation by continuing to put pressure on the government,” student and teacher unions said in a joint statement released Monday. Student association leader Ryad Rani said it was essential to keep up the pressure. “We’re not just fighting for ourselves. We’re fighting for teachers, for their working conditions,” he said. The government has announced measures including the gradual replacement of an online selection platform to access higher education, as well as financial means for some of the worst-off schools. But students say this is not enough. Unions are not happy either, with one leader saying on Monday that a government pledge to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent on top of a standard adjustment for inflation was “crumbs”. They have called for a new day of strikes and protests on November 17. Around 575,000 people demonstrated across the country during cost-of-living strikes and protests last Thursday, according to authorities. Unions put the number at 1.5 million. nigeria.title: Iran calls on US to meet its demands to end war
nigeria.description: Iran on Tuesday urged the United States to meet its demands in a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, after President Donald Trump spoke of “positive momentum” to end their eight-month war. “The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iran’s IRNA news agency. “The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran’s demands and conditions — which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table.” Tehran has proposed reopening Hormuz, which it has blockaded since the start of the war, within two days in return for Washington meeting a raft of conditions. These include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Trump, whose Republican party last week lost midterm elections in part due to the war, said on Monday that there was “positive momentum” towards ending the conflict after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House. In a post on social media, Trump reiterated that the US was “locked and loaded” but said further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo”. “We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said. Diplomatic efforts, led by Qatar and Pakistan, are underway to find a resolution to the war, which broke out in late February when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s active telecom lines hit 200m as 5G share crosses 5%
nigeria.description: …As Internet data usage falls to 1.73 terabytes in September By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnections in 2024. Latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, showed that active lines increased by about 2.9 million, from 197.4 million in August. The September figure of 200,337,097 subscriptions was up from 197,416,694 in August. Teledensity rose to 92.41 per cent from 91.07 per cent. The NCC defines teledensity as the number of active telephone connections per 100 inhabitants. It measures subscriptions rather than unique users, as one person may have more than one line. The data showed that 4G remained the largest share of mobile connections at 54.37 per cent in September. 2G accounted for 36.42 per cent, while 3G made up 4.16 per cent. 5G’s share increased to 5.05 per cent from 4.92 per cent in August. Internet subscriptions also grew, rising to 160.9 million from 158.5 million in August. Broadband subscriptions increased to 128 million in September from 126.2 million the previous month, while broadband penetration rose to 59.05 per cent from 58.22 per cent. However, total internet data usage declined to 1.73 million terabytes in September from 1.76 million terabytes in August. Mobile number porting increased during the month, with 1,603 subscribers switching networks, compared with 1,111 in August. MTN recorded 854 incoming ports, Airtel 580, Globacom 165 and Vitel four. T2 recorded none. The figures also showed that the telecommunications industry’s contribution to gross domestic product, GDP, rose to 9.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 9.19 per cent in the first quarter. Fixed broadband infrastructure expanded, with Fibre to the X (FTTX) subscriptions rising to 401,666 in the third quarter from 319,735 in the second quarter. The NCC’s FTTX category covers fibre connections to homes, offices, streets, hubs and other locations, including subscriptions from internet service providers and fixed or private network operators. nigeria.title: New Israel parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot seeks government
nigeria.description: Israel’s new parliament will be sworn in Tuesday, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu set to lose his majority even as rival Gadi Eisenkot still works to form a new government. President Isaac Herzog will deliver a speech at 4:00 pm (1400 GMT) for the swearing-in of the 120-seat parliament, in which neither Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc nor Eisenkot’s opposition will hold a majority. The opposition hopes to use its newfound legislative power to move quickly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas, the deadliest day in Israel’s history. Herzog on Sunday gave Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to cobble together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Ahead of the parliament opening, Eisenkot’s party announced progress in naming people to seek key positions. The opposition will put forward Matan Kahana — like Eisenkot a former senior military figure — as speaker of the parliament, Eisenkot’s Yashar party said. Avigdor Lieberman, a right-wing opposition leader who has played a key role in deciding who can enter the government, will be nominated as chair of the foreign affairs and defence committee. The opposition’s choice for speaker would need to secure a larger number of votes than anyone backed by Netanyahu’s bloc, which has been trying to push back a vote on the speaker. The newly formed government would need 61 votes to be approved to take office. Eisenkot could secure the threshold with support from Arab-Israeli lawmakers, who secured a record number of seats on the back of anger in the minority community over Netanyahu’s hard-right government. But Lieberman had been clear he would not allow Eisenkot to rely on Arab-Israelis to come to power. He has instead proposed an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, despite his years of bitter denunciations of the community for its singular priority on maintaining an exemption from mandatory military service. Eisenkot’s core opposition bloc has fewer seats than Netanyahu at 48, but would achieve a majority if the 19 Arab-Israeli lawmakers either enter the government or, more likely, vote for it without joining. The two ultra-Orthodox parties, with 13 seats, could also crown Eisenkot if they ditch their long alliance with Netanyahu, who backed the exemption from military service without enshrining it fully into law. An alliance with either group would likely be fragile. Arab-Israelis are likely to object if Eisenkot carries out another major offensive in Gaza. Eisenkot has largely backed Netanyahu’s war decisions, although he has vowed to crack down on extremist settlers in the West Bank who have been attacking and stealing from Palestinians with virtual impunity. nigeria.title: UFC chief declines Trump’s White House job offer
nigeria.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump’s — apparently jovial — offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post — but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was “only kidding.” The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room. “So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?” Trump said. “Thank you for the offer, sir — for the offer, I have no, no — I do not want to be in politics,” White replied. Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: “I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody.” The press secretary’s post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job. Trump’s announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to “violent Fighter and Warrior” White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party’s stunning midterm elections defeat. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year. But there was also some skepticism about the president’s announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking. – ‘Beat the hell out of you’ – Leading out White to the podium on Monday, Trump said he had been “having a little fun.” “He’s a great guy,” Trump told the room full of reporters. “The only problem is he’ll talk for a little while and then he’s going to beat the hell out of you.” Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon — the ring used for UFC fights. “I’ve always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?” he joked — before quickliy adding: “I have zero political aspirations.” White added that “the last 24 hours of my life has been insane” since Trump made the announcement. Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: “I don’t tell the president ‘no’ to anything… I didn’t want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first.” Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang. nigeria.title: I give kudos to people who sent me to jail; it’s like school – Orji Kalu

Kalu said rather than regret his incarceration, he considers it an experience that changed his understanding of life and helped him develop a different outlook. The former Abia State governor made the remarks during an interview on Arise Television on Monday. Explaining why he was grateful for the experience, Kalu said, “It made me more humble. nigeria.title: 2027: Tinubu will win, he has no competition — Orji Kalu

On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Whether taking the government to task on “20 Years to Come” or offering uplifting anthems like “ Chukwu Okike ”, Phyno proves why he remains a definitive voice in African hip-hop. ﻿ Ty Bello: I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb Creative powerhouse Ty Bello delivers a massive double-album listening experience with I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb . Split into two distinct spiritual volumes, the expansive project captures both the bold, triumphant authority of worship and its quiet, intimate moments. ﻿ I Speak Lion leans into explosive, high-energy sounds designed to spark courage, featuring powerful pairings with Sunmisola Agbebi , Greatman Takit , and Limoblaze . For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the idea presents an opportunity to examine the traditions women inherit, the rituals they observe and the choices they make when dressing for themselves. The collection is built around two identities: The Devotee and The Rebel. They are not opposing personalities so much as two ways of relating to ceremony. The Devotee embraces its rituals. The garments give form to this conversation. The Cloister Dress is paired with the Banner Dress, while the Manor Jumpsuit is placed alongside the Assembly Set. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. He said he returned from his studies abroad to a Nigeria where his peers were filing into banking, oil and gas, and where technology was largely seen as a foreign game. Ekeh, who studied Economics in India, said he was discouraged from pursuing a postgraduate degree in Computer Science in Europe because of the prevailing perception then that Africa might have little need for computers over the next 35 years, potentially leaving him frustrated. He subsequently opted for a postgraduate degree in Risk Management before pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Law (LLM) at London Guildhall University. He recalled that he could not sit his final law examinations because he had diverted his tuition fees into his passion for technology entrepreneurship. He also disclosed that he had fended off recruitment attempts by international technology companies that had sought to hire him before his return to Africa. “I chose the road not taken,” he told the conference. “It was corporate suicide in the eyes of my parents and many others. According to him, his vision was to create a Nigerian and, by extension, an African IT identity. Recalling the launch of his first company, Task Systems Ltd, over 35 years ago, the company that pioneered desktop publishing and computer graphics in Nigeria. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. entertainment.title: History in Morocco! How Nigeria’s Flamingos Won the World Cup
entertainment.description: The Flamingos celebrate on stage with green and white confetti as they lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy. History was made in Rabat as the Flamingos of Nigeria conquered global football at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Under head coach Akeem Busari , the team executed an extraordinary seven-match campaign at the finals, overcoming an early setback to claim six consecutive victories and become the first African nation to lift any FIFA women’s international trophy. Midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku earned individual recognition by winning the FIFA Golden Ball as the Player of the Tournament alongside Player of the Match honors in the final. The squad also displayed exceptional attacking breadth, scoring goals through eight different players across seven matches at the finals while registering over 100 goal attempts. Oluebube Umejiaku poses with the FIFA Golden Ball and Player of the Match awards following Nigeria’s World Cup triumph. Here is the match-by-match breakdown of how Nigeria navigated the African qualifiers, powered through the World Cup group stage, defeated multi-time global champions in the knockouts, and clinched the ultimate trophy in Morocco. Nigeria’s Flamingos celebrate becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in Rabat. Phase 1: The African Qualifying Journey Nigeria entered the African U-17 World Cup qualifying campaign in the second round, establishing dominance in home-and-away aggregate ties across West Africa. The Flamingos opened their qualification run with an emphatic 5–0 away victory in Guinea, led by team captain Harmony Chidi ’s first-half hat-trick alongside goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Mary Dunstan . They followed up with a 7–0 victory in the home leg in Ogun State to complete a 12–0 aggregate shutout. The Flamingos celebrate on the pitch following their matchday four fixture at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. In the final qualifying round, Nigeria established a three-goal lead in Monrovia by defeating Liberia 4–1, thanks to a brace from Harmony Chidi and goals from Shakirat Moshood and Peace Effiong . entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. sports.description: Arsenal 31yo makes World 11, teammate narrowly misses out David Raya has become the first Arsenal player to feature in the FIFPRO World 11 since Thierry Henry, with a couple of his teammates only narrowly missing out. Photo via FIFPRO on Instagram After tallying up 19,806 votes from professional men’s footballers across 73 countries, FIFPRO named their World 11 on Monday night, with Arsenal’s David Raya making the cut. Raya is the first Arsenal player to be included in the World 11 since Thierry Henry in 2006, and he’s one of just two Premier League players in the 2026 side alongside Erling Haaland (or three if you include Rodri ). It wasn’t a close race in the goalkeeper position, with Raya receiving more than 2,500 more votes than his nearest competitor. In fact, the goalkeeper received more votes than anyone else in the entire lineup, with over half of the voters picking him. FIFPRO World 11 for 2026 Arsenal were rather unlucky not to have at least one more player in the lineup. Gabriel Magalhaes received the second-most votes of any centre-back, only behind Pau Cubarsi of Barcelona and Spain. But the award organisers opted to select a team with only three defenders, one of whom was a left-back, and another a right-back. So with only one centre-back spot in the side, Gabriel missed out. If the team used a formation that a real football team might use, Gabriel would have been included, as it’s very hard to think of any team in world football that only uses one centre-back. William Saliba was also very close to making the cut, as both Gabriel and Saliba finished within 1,000 votes of Cubarsi. Raya sent a message to the voters after receiving his award, saying : “Thank you guys for voting me into the FIFPRO World 11. It’s incredible how you guys have voted for me. sports.title: ‘Y’all wish’ – Luka Doncic responds to Atlanta Hawks heckler with reminder their biggest mistake
sports.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Even eight years later, Luka Doncic has not forgotten about how the Atlanta Hawks disrespected him in the NBA Draft. Doncic is now the next superstar for the Los Angeles Lakers, taking over the mantle from LeBron James following his departure earlier this summer. But before he arrived in Los Angeles, Doncic was the name and face of the Dallas Mavericks for seven years, a position carved out for him on the night of the 2018 NBA Draft. Luka Doncic pokes fun at Atlanta Hawks fan over 2018 NBA Draft trade During the Los Angeles Lakers’ win against the Atlanta Hawks, Luka Doncic got into a heated exchange with some hecklers sitting courtside. Doncic used the back-and-forth as an opportunity to remind them that the Hawks made a mistake giving him up in the 2018 NBA Draft. Luka Doncic: “You all wish you would’ve had me. You all wish, huh?” Fan #1: “We had you.” Fan #2: “No, we don’t. I’ve never wanted you.” Fan #3: “I wish we did; I do.” Luka Doncic: “You know you could have had me.” Fan #3: “He’s right.” Of course, Doncic is referencing the draft-night trade the Atlanta Hawks made in 2018. The Hawks had the #3 overall pick in the 2018 NBA Draft, with Doncic being expected to be selected by the Hawks. However, on the night, the Hawks traded the draft rights to Luka Doncic (whom they picked at #3) to the Dallas Mavericks in exchange for the draft rights to Trae Young and a 2019 protected first-round pick that turned out to be Cam Reddish. Fast-forward eight years, and the Hawks have fully given up on Trae Young, trading him to the Washington Wizards earlier this year after an eight-year stint that saw them reach the Eastern Conference Finals just once. As for Cam Reddish, he never adapted to the NBA and found himself outside of the league following the conclusion of the 2024-25 NBA season. In the early days of the trade, many had suggested that the Mavericks and Hawks had pulled off a rare win-win trade. However, following Young’s decline as a superstar, the consensus became clear – the Mavericks had pulled off a coup for Doncic. Unfortunately for the Mavericks, they didn’t get to reap the rewards of their clever trade, as Nico Harrison would trade Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie, and just one first-round pick. Now, the Lakers have emerged as the ultimate winners of a trade in 2018 that never included them in the first place. sports.title: Konate reveals Kylian Mbappe’s reaction to missing out on Ballon d’Or: ‘He more than deserved it’
sports.description: Konate reveals Kylian Mbappe’s reaction to missing out on Ballon d’Or: ‘He more than deserved it’ Kylian Mbappe has wasted little time moving on from his Ballon d’Or disappointment, despite finishing just 28 points behind Harry Kane in the voting. The Real Madrid forward came close to claiming the individual award , but Kane ultimately emerged as the winner. Mbappe has not spoken extensively about the result since the ceremony, with his attention returning to club football. However, France and Real Madrid teammate Ibrahima Konate has offered his insight into how the forward has reacted, suggesting the defeat has not affected his focus or motivation. Konate explains why the defeat hurt Mbappe Konate, who signed for Real Madrid this past summer on a free transfer from Liverpool, suggested that the narrow defeat was particularly difficult for the forward because he believed the award was within his reach. Konate explains why Mbappe was hurt after missing out on the Ballon d’or. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) “He more than deserved the Ballon d’Or, which is why it’s tough for him not to have won it.” The Real Madrid defender added, as per Defensa Central , that “He’s in very good spirits. He’s ready for whatever comes his way and is working hard.” Mbappe answers disappointment with goals Mbappe, on his part, has made a strong start to life after the ceremony. He scored in each of the club’s three subsequent fixtures, finding the net against Racing Santander, AEK Athens and Valencia. Mbappe opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 3-0 victory over Racing, struck in the 3-2 Champions League win against AEK and scored again during the 3-0 success at Valencia. Kylian Mbappe is still enjoying a great run of form. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Notably, the sequence of his form is actually giving him a useful platform for the remainder of the campaign. Rather than allowing the Ballon d’Or result to dominate his season, Mbappe can focus on collective trophies and performances that will influence his next opportunity to win it. UCL success could influence Mbappe’s next Ballon d’Or bid The absence of a major men’s international tournament in 2027 places additional importance on club football in the next Ballon d’Or race. Mbappe will therefore have a significant incentive to help Real Madrid compete for the Champions League and deliver consistently across the season. Indeed, the likes of Lamine Yamal will still be in contention, but if Real Madrid win major trophies under Jose Mourinho, especially the Champions League, Mbappe’s chances of challenging for the Ballon d’Or next year will undoubtedly increase.

sports.title: Hungarian federation issues Dominik Szoboszlai update as Liverpool left sweating on his fitness
sports.description: Hungarian federation issues Dominik Szoboszlai update as Liverpool left sweating on his fitness The Hungarian FA has issued an update on the fitness of Dominik Szoboszlai ahead of their upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures. There is an injury concern over the midfielder after he sprained his knee in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday, with Andoni Iraola unsure as to whether or not the 26-year-old would be able to represent his country during this international window. The Magyars are away to Georgia this coming Saturday and then host Northern Ireland three days later in what could be a straight shootout for promotion to League A on the final matchday. Szoboszlai decision to be left to the ‘last minute’ On Tuesday, the Hungarian FA published an update via X in which they confirmed that a decision on Szoboszlai won’t be taken until the latest possible opportunity. They stated: ‘Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations. Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible. ‘However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute.’ (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Liverpool will need Szoboszlai during frantic fixture period As captain of his country, the 26-year-old will no doubt be striving to prove his fitness in time for the match against Georgia on Saturday, or at least be in a position to play against Northern Ireland. However, those of a Liverpool perspective will surely be hoping that Szoboszlai isn’t risked in either game if he isn’t 100% fit to feature, as he’ll be very much needed at Anfield going into the unforgiving winter schedule. The Reds still have 11 more matches to play in 2026, starting with a grudge fixture at home to Manchester United on Sunday week, and squad depth and rotation will be essential during that hectic period in the run-up to Christmas and New Year’s. Having only recently returned from a thigh issue, Andoni Iraola will be hoping that this doesn’t turn into a season of frequent interruptions for the usually dependable Hungarian, who before this autumn hadn’t missed a game through injury since February 2024 ( Transfermarkt ). sports.title: “There’s No Drama” – Mirra Andreeva Breaks Silence On WTA Finals ‘Diva’ Controversy With Jessica Pegula
sports.description: Mirra Andreeva © Instagram/_mirraandreeva_ Mirra Andreeva recently addressed the controversy surrounding Jessica Pegula’s ‘diva’ remark at the WTA Finals after the incident caught fans’ attention. Pegula’s private conversation with her coach Mark Knowles was unknowingly broadcast during a practice session at Indian Wells. The American tennis player was heard making comments about Andreeva and her coach Conchita Martínez. Pegula slammed Andreeva’s on-court behavior, calling her a “diva” who needed to be “humbled.” She also took a swipe at Andreeva’s coach for encouraging the French Open champion’s behavior. “I think she’s a nice girl, but she’s a diva; she needs to be humbled,” Pegula said via Tennis World. During her appearance at the WTA Finals, Andreeva broke her silence on the controversy, saying she appreciated that Pegula approached her just a few hours after the incident to apologize (via Christian Court’s X). “I mean, I really appreciated that she came up to me on the same day. I feel, I think maybe a couple of hours just went by and she, you know, she approached me. I would probably like to keep what she said between her and me, but yeah, I really appreciated that she just came up to me. Obviously, she apologized, so there’s no drama or anything behind it. Now we’re able to laugh about it, so I think that’s the most important.” After being seen off by Coco Gauff, Pegula will face Marta Kostyuk in the next group match at the WTA Finals. Mirra Andreeva opens her WTA Finals campaign with a win over Elina Svitolina Mirra Andreeva made her singles debut at the WTA Finals during the 2026 edition in Indian Wells, California. She saw off Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-0. Andreeva saved all six break points she faced and held her serve throughout the match. The clash featured a 12-year-and-229-day age gap between the players, the biggest at the WTA Finals since Venus Williams locked horns with Caroline Garcia in 2017. Andreeva was beaten by Svitolina at the Australian Open earlier this year. After her win over Svitolina, Andreeva reflected on her 2025 Indian Wells quarterfinals win over the Ukrainian, where she dominated 7-5, 6-3. “I was trying to think about was that she beat me in Australia earlier this year,” Andreeva said via Rediff . “I really tried not to think about the match we had last year on these courts. I remember how I was playing when I beat her here, but I knew it would be a tricky match. She’s an amazing player. I’m just very happy I was able to get through the match.” Mirra Andreeva will next face Aryna Sabalenka in the group stage of the WTA Finals. Sabalenka overcame Karolina Muchova 7-6(2), 7-5 at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. As such, the Barcelona coaching staff believes they could have him available at the for the clash on 22 November at the Spotify Camp Nou. In fact, the report adds that such has been Olmo’s progress that he could even have been available had Barcelona played a midweek fixture before the Villarreal match. sports.title: Inter target Calhanoglu renewal by Christmas but wage remains sticking point
sports.description: Inter target Calhanoglu renewal by Christmas but wage remains sticking point Inter and Hakan Calhanoglu are working towards a contract renewal, but they still need to agree on wages before he can sign. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via TuttoMercatoWeb , both sides want to continue together, and an agreement could be reached by Christmas if the terms fall into place. The 32-year-old’s current deal runs until June 2027 and pays him around €6.5m net per season. MILAN, ITALY – AUGUST 22: Hakan Calhanoglu of Internazionale celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and AC Monza at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on August 22, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Calhanoglu’s Inter contract talks The renewal talks follow a tense few months. During Inter’s pre-season tour of Australia in August, Calhanoglu said he was surprised there had been no talks over an extension. He insisted he was still attached to Milan, Inter and the fans, but said his future was in the club’s hands. He was also reportedly worried that he was no longer seen as central to Inter’s plans, even though Cristian Chivu has backed him throughout and he remains key to the team. MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 10: Hakan Calhanoglu of FC Internazionale Milano celebrates scoring his team’s second goal from the penalty spot during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Parma Calcio at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 10, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The main obstacle is money. Calhanoglu wants a new two-year contract with the salary of a top player. Inter, meanwhile, want to reduce the fixed part of their wage bill, especially for a player of his age who has had recent fitness problems. Talks are now open, and both sides will need to compromise to reach a deal.

technology.title: Royal Navy stands up first autonomous boat squadron
technology.description: Britain’s Royal Navy has formally commissioned its first uncrewed boat squadron, operating seaborne drones on front-line operations as part of its “Hybrid Navy” strategy. The force says the 1 st Autonomous Squadron officially entered active service on November 5 at a ceremony in Portsmouth Naval Base. It comprises around 180 personnel, about the same as a Type 23 frigate, split into two watches to enable operations around the clock. This active squadron replaces Project Beehive, the navy’s experimental program to build a fleet of autonomous and remotely operated vessels, through which it obtained 20 uncrewed boats from UK-based Kraken Technology Group. technology.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. The product has become particularly useful since Anthropic's Mythos model, and similar AI offerings, made it possible to quickly find more software bugs and flaws and overwhelmed tech teams whose patching apparatus was not set up to handle hundreds of montly CVEs. Live Protect currently works on some of Cisco's datacenter switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. "Expect this to be a major investment area," Schultz added. ®

science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. science.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. science.description: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559 located about 30 million light-years from Earth. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space. science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . science.description: 1 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) This Hall-effect thruster, shown being tested at Glenn Research Center, turns electricity and inert gas into force that could propel a spacecraft. Orbion Space Technology was founded to bring the high efficiency of these thrusters to small commercial satellites, and the company sought the center’s help to make that a reality. Credit: NASA Mid-power (3-7 kW) Hall effect thruster systems have been identified by government and industry stakeholders as critical capabilities for satellite, defense, and exploration missions. Given the need for this capability, NASA is launching the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge. The NASA AMPERE Challenge invites U.S. commercial companies to develop and demonstrate mid-power Hall effect thruster prototypes. Through this challenge, NASA aims to accelerate the maturation of electric propulsion capabilities, validate real-world performance in NASA test facilities, and build the foundation needed to support future NASA and commercial missions. The challenge is open to companies incorporated in and maintaining a primary place of business in the United States. Award: $500,000 in total prizes. science.title: La NASA destina un millón de dólares al reto estudiantil Base Lunar
science.description: Representación artística en la que se muestran astronautas, hábitats, rovers, sistemas de energía y operaciones de carga que permiten mantener actividades humanas continuadas en la Base Lunar, situada cerca del Polo Sur lunar. El domingo 8 de noviembre de 2026, la NASA anunció la convocatoria del reto estudiantil Base Lunar, dotado con un millón de dólares, durante un acto de MAX POWER celebrado en el Complejo de Visitantes del Centro Espacial Kennedy, en Florida. En el marco de una edad de oro de la ciencia, la competición invita a equipos de estudiantes de escuelas secundarias y centros de educación superior de Estados Unidos a aportar diseños para la Base Lunar. “Buscamos estudiantes dispuestos a pensar de forma creativa, a trabajar en equipo y a abordar problemas reales relacionados con el futuro de la NASA en la Luna”, dijo el administrador de la NASA, Jared Isaacman. “No hace falta esperar hasta la graduación para contribuir. La curiosidad, la creatividad y la voluntad de afrontar problemas difíciles sin respuestas obvias son precisamente las cualidades que necesitamos mientras construimos lo que viene a continuación”. La NASA está construyendo la Base Lunar, donde los astronautas vivirán, trabajarán y explorarán la región del Polo Sur lunar. La presencia humana permanente en la Luna allana el camino para futuras misiones tripuladas a Marte y requiere talento procedente de diversos sectores y ámbitos. “A medida que construimos y diseñamos los cimientos de la Base Lunar, queremos aprovechar todo el ingenio y la innovación para tener en cuenta cada aspecto que nuestros exploradores puedan necesitar para vivir y trabajar allí”, afirmó Carlos García-Galán, director del programa Base Lunar. “Los estudiantes aportan precisamente las ideas audaces que estamos buscando, y estoy deseando descubir su enfoque. En definitiva, la Base Lunar es para ellos, las personas que vivirán en un mundo en el que los seres humanos estarán en la Luna para quedarse”. Este reto, que consta de varias fases, refuerza el compromiso de la NASA con el desarrollo de las competencias técnicas del personal aeroespacial del futuro. Los equipos de estudiantes diseñarán soluciones innovadoras para la Base Lunar en seis categorías: generación y almacenamiento de energía, construcción, sistemas de soporte vital, movilidad en la superficie, redes de comunicaciones y seguridad de los astronautas. La iniciativa ofrece a los participantes la oportunidad de adquirir las aptitudes necesarias para una carrera en la industria espacial, al tiempo que contribuye al avance de nuevos conceptos tecnológicos para la Base Lunar. Los participantes deben inscribirse en el reto a través de la plataforma NASA STEM Gateway , en inglés. El plazo de inscripción está abierto hasta el 25 de enero de 2027. “Los estudiantes son la siguiente generación de exploradores e innovadores.
